sections.title: How does the 6 sided dice probability calculator work?
sections.html:
The 6 sided dice probability calculator takes the values in the form, applies the relationship described below and reports number of faces in the results panel.

Working from the top of the form: you choose the option that describes your case (the I want to get); then you type in the total number of dice, the dice value I want to get, the value (Choose the conditions - Game rules) and the value (Choose the conditions - Game rules).

The arithmetic runs locally each time an input changes. The page knows which values you have given it and which it still has to derive, so the results panel is never stale.

Because the equation can be rearranged for each of its variables, the page also runs backwards. Leave the box you want to know empty, fill in the rest, and it solves for the missing one instead. That is useful when you know the answer you need rather than the inputs you have.

sections.title: The formula behind the 6 sided dice probability calculator
sections.html:
The page rests on a handful of relationships. Each one can be rearranged for any of its variables, which is what makes the calculator work in both directions:

Number of faces=1 ÷ dice probability
The probability of getting the side value you want in all dice=(total number of dice, dice probability)
The probability of getting any value from the dice=(total number of dice, dice probability)
The probability=(total number of dice, dice probability × (number of faces − the dice value I want to get + 1))
The probability=(total number of dice, dice probability × the dice value I want to get)
The probability=(number of faces, total number of dice, target number of dice (X), dice probability, the value, ...or, ...or, ...or, ...or, ...or, ...or, ...or, ...or, ...or)

Read it as an ordinary equation. Where a word appears instead of a letter, it is the label of one of the boxes in the form; where a function appears, it is the usual mathematical meaning of that function.

sections.title: What is a worked example?
sections.html:
The form opens with a complete set of values: Number of faces = 6, I want to get set to All dice with the same face/side value, How many target values do you want? set to 1 and ...or = 0. Straight away the calculator returns Dice probability = 0.1667.

Those are real numbers produced by the same engine that runs when you press Calculate, so you can change any single box afterwards and watch the answer move from this starting point.

  1. Enter the values listed above, matching the units each box asks for.
  2. Read off the result. Any field you leave empty is the one the calculator solves for.
  3. Sanity-check the number against the relationship: Dice probability = 0.1667 should be roughly the size you expected from Number of faces = 6 and I want to get set to All dice with the same face/side value.

sections.title: When should you use it?
sections.html:
The 6 sided dice probability calculator earns its place in the middle of a task, not instead of one. It is most useful when:

  • Checking a result a piece of software produced
  • Deciding how much confidence a sample really supports
  • Turning raw numbers into something you can quote
  • Any time the same 4 figures keep coming back — the total number of dice, the dice value I want to get and the value — and you would rather not repeat the arithmetic by hand each time.

sections.title: How do you get a reliable answer?
sections.html:
• Write the answer down with its unit. A bare number copied into a report later is exactly where units get lost.
  • Leave the field you want solved for empty rather than guessing at it. Filling every box tells the calculator you already know the answer.
  • Change one input at a time when you are exploring. Two simultaneous changes make it impossible to tell which one moved the result.
  • Keep the units you enter consistent. Mixing centimetres into a field that expects metres is the single most common way to get an answer that is out by a factor of a hundred.

sections.title: What else is worth knowing?
sections.html:
• Filling in more than one box is fine. The most recently edited field is the one treated as known, so you can switch direction without reloading.
  • Answers that depend on a drop-down reflect the option you picked, not a range. Switching to a neighbouring option is the quickest way to see how much that factor matters.
  • Some options are backed by reference tables that ship with the page, so the values are fixed data rather than a live lookup.
  • Fields that are still blank are exactly the ones the calculator has not yet been given, so the results panel is a reliable map of what is missing.

faq.q: What does the 6 sided dice probability calculator work out?
faq.a: It returns number of faces, derived from the total number of dice, the dice value I want to get and the value. Every field in the form feeds the same relationship: press Calculate once and changing any of them updates the result immediately, with no page reload.

faq.q: What do I need to enter to use the 6 sided dice probability calculator?
faq.a: The form asks for the total number of dice, the dice value I want to get, the value and the ...or, which is 17 fields in total. Each one is labelled with what it means and, where relevant, the unit it expects. Anything you leave blank is treated as the value to solve for.
Yes. Each variable in the relationship can be the one being solved for: fill in the answer you are aiming at, leave the field you want empty, and the calculator inverts the equation for you.

faq.q: How much do the drop-down choices change the answer?
faq.a: There are several choices to make (2 in total), and each one selects a different case rather than scaling the result. Switching a single option and watching the result is the fastest way to see how much that choice is worth.

With the values the page starts from, the calculator reports Dice probability = 0.1667. Treat that as a reference point rather than a recommendation: it exists so you can tell at a glance whether your own inputs are on the same scale.

faq.q: Is the 6 sided dice probability calculator free to use?
faq.a: Yes — no account, no sign-up and no limit on how many times you run it. The arithmetic happens in your browser, so the values you type are not sent anywhere.
